Follow on X Multiple Authors Oct 2, 2026, 11:00 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and moneylines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 4. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills (-6.5, 48.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, New York Josh Allen and the Bills split their series with the Patriots last season. Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire The Buffalo Bills , the AFC favorite to reach the Super Bowl, will host last season's AFC Super Bowl representative, the New England Patriots , in a matchup of AFC East rivals Sunday. The Patriots will need game plan answers on both sides of the ball to counter the Bills' high-scoring offense, and they'll have to create a more defined passing game without A.J. Brown (ankle) on the field. I like the Bills to win and cover in this one, and in a divisional game with this level of coaching and familiarity, I'll take the under on the total. Let's check out both clubs, and I'll add some props at the end to play, too. NFL betting • Best bets for Sunday: Cincy in danger? • Burrow passes Allen as MVP fave | Odds • Why Lawrence is the best MVP value • Betting favorites go 14-1 in Week 9 • Odds for Week 10 games | Early bets • Super Bowl odds: Jaguars move up • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Bills have the ball: In their Week 3 win over the Chargers, the Bills failed to control offensive tempo, and they turned the ball over. It happens in this league. But don't let one game change the narrative on an explosive Bills offense leading the NFL in scoring (33.7 PPG) and producing top-10 numbers in both passing and rushing. Quarterback Josh Allen will see heavy single-high coverage from New England (both man and zone), which creates opportunities for the Bills to scheme for crossing concepts and big-play throws on deep over routes, and they can also attack the seams with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The man matchup to watch to here is DJ Moore against Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), if the Patriots corner is up for the game. Best versus best. And let's not forget the offensive balance the Bills have with running back James Cook III , who has produced back-to-back games with at least 135 yards rushing, against a New England defense allowing 4.8 YPC. The question I always have for teams versus Allen, given his dual-threat ability, is how much man coverage can you play? And what is your answer for Allen as a runner in the low red zone? Let's see how the Patriots counter, as Allen has rushed for two scores in all three games played this season. He's the league's ultimate difference-maker. When the Patriots have the ball: Quarterback Drake Maye has made some reckless decisions with the ball, throwing a league-high six interceptions and registering a 45.9 QBR (25th in the league). But I'm not going to put this all on Maye, as the Patriots' wide receiver group is lacking juice and matchup edges. With Brown on IR, who is the boundary X to win the one-on-ones? The tape shows us that the New England wideouts aren't creating separation at a high rate. The key here is for Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to scheme more defined throws -- while having answers to pressure -- versus a Bills defense that has been more zone-heavy (65.9% of opponent dropbacks). Maye is going to see split-safety coverage. Lift the safeties here and create those middle-of-the-field voids for the quarterback to drive the ball. More importantly, the Patriots need to generate some run-game efficiency with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to get the Bills out of two-deep coverage. The Patriots are averaging 3.9 YPC (20th in the league) with an explosive run rate of 8.2% (25th). No question on the numbers here. They are down. Let's see how McDaniels game-plans for Jim Leonhard and the Bills' new defensive scheme to get his QB rolling again. And it wouldn't surprise me if the Patriots try to muddy this one up with a ball control/play-action script. Now, let's get to some prop bets ... James Cook III is coming off two straight big rushing performances and is averaging 6.0 YPC. AP Photo/Adrian Kraus James Cook III rushing yards OVER 88.5 (-111) As mentioned, Cook has rushed for 135-plus in two straight, and he's averaging 19.3 carries per game. Plus, Cook has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season. Take the steady volume and the explosive-play ability here. Hunter Henry receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-110) Henry has topped the 31-yard mark just once this season, and he was held to just one reception in the Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. However, I see the tight end as an answer to the two-high zone coverage of the Bills. Henry can be the outlet for Maye, while also pressing the seams. DJ Moore receptions OVER 3.5 (-133) The juice isn't friendly on this one, but that's a low reception total for Moore. In the two full games Moore has played (he left Week 2 early with an injury), he had at least five receptions in both. Look for the Bills to use motion to deploy Moore, getting him free access off the ball versus man coverage. Matt Bowen 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Moneyline 1-2 -1.1 Spread 6-3 +2.3 Total 1-8 -7.1 Passing props 0-2 -2.0 Receiving props 4-7 -3.4 Rushing props 5-4 +0.4 Rushing and receiving props 1-2 -1.1 Touchdown props 2-6 -1.1 Teasers 3-0 +2.1 Parlays 0-1 -1.0 Overall 23-35 -11.9 Solak's plays Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has produced 463 total yards this season and could be in for another big game Sunday. Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire Detroit Lions -3.5 (-112) at Carolina Panthers It's important to watch the forecast for this game as we get closer to kickoff. There's a good chance of rain showers Sunday night, and we know that Jared Goff 's performance as a passer can be impacted more by bad weather, given his smaller hands. But I still feel comfortable taking this bet at this number because of the Panthers' injury issues. Both starting cornerbacks are expected to miss this game, which all but precludes Carolina from playing man coverage against Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams . If the Panthers take a zone-heavy approach, expect Jahmyr Gibbs to run wild -- heck, expect Gibbs to run wild anyway, as the Panthers are giving up more rushing yards per game to running backs than any other defense. Have I mentioned the Panthers' passing defense is also among the league worst against tight ends? The Lions have Carolina outgunned offensively, and I'm not sure Bryce Young can keep scoring pace. Receiver Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable, three starting offensive linemen ( Ikem Ekwonu , Damien Lewis and Taylor Moton ) are out, and a key backup ( Monroe Freeling ) is in concussion protocol. Detroit's defense is extremely gettable through the air, but the Lions have enough pass rush power to generate sacks and turnovers such that the Panthers can't keep this shootout within one score. Los Angeles Rams -3 (-115) at Philadelphia Eagles Editor's Picks Top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 4 Mike Clay NFL Week 4 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game Early bets for Week 4: Four games to target right away ESPN 2 Related I would only take this line at -3 (up to -120) and not buy the hook, so move quickly here. DeVonta Smith missed practice Thursday with his hamstring injury, which officially moves him into the "seriously questionable" category as we approach Sunday. I already leaned to the Rams' side with a healthy Smith. If he can't go, the Eagles' receiver corps will feature Dontayvion Wicks , first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown against the loaded Rams secondary. Remember, pass-catching tight end Dallas Goedert is also out with a knee injury. The Eagles' defense had a brutal night last Monday against the Chicago Bears ' passing attack, regularly suffering communication issues as the Bears sent receivers in motion. They get another motion-heavy passing attack in Sean McVay's Rams offense, which gets Puka Nacua back at a critical time -- at 1-2, the Rams need a road win to prevent the sirens from screaming in their Super Bowl-aspiring season. They also have a vengeance play here, as they gave up a big second-half lead to the Eagles last season ... then lost the game on a would-be game-winning field goal that was blocked by Jordan Davis . The Eagles simply have too many personnel deficiencies to ignore against a team as deep and talented as the Rams. Get this line before Smith news pushes it higher before kickoff. Miami Dolphins team total points UNDER 13.5 (-115) Minnesota Vikings DC Brian Flores is calling defense for the first time against his old team. He has downplayed the importance of facing Miami, but I'd imagine the leaders in the locker room know how big of a game this is for their top-flight coordinator. I also think this is about as big of a mismatch as we will see this season. The Dolphins are without running back De'Von Achane , who provided much-needed game-breaking ability from the running back spot. Without him, the Dolphins' best chance for chunk gains will come from the passing game, which is a scary proposition against Flores' blitz-heavy approach. Bobby Slowik, the new offensive coordinator in Miami, lost his job in Houston in large part due to predictable protection rules that were easily exploited by opposing defensive coordinators -- and no coach has been better attacking the Mike Shanahan system in pass protection than Flores. I'm tracking under 13.5 at -115 for a full unit and under 7.5 points at +285 for a half unit. A shutout at 13-1 would be fun, but that's too short of a price to take seriously. Omarion Hampton rushing yards UNDER 45.5 (-109) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Hampton's share of carries took a hit last week, as he saw 57.7% of the designed rushes after holding 76.7% and 75.0% in the first two weeks of the season, respectively. The Los Angeles Chargers wanted to get Keaton Mitchell more involved as they looked for any sort of juice on offense, and it was a better day for the running game overall. I expect a time share moving forward. But it will be a tough test against the Seattle Seahawks , who boast the best run-defending line in football. There might be no greater mismatch in Week 4 than the Chargers' interior offensive line against defensive tackles Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams . If the Chargers are to find any success on the ground, they'll need to get the ball to the boundary -- those are the Mitchell plays, not the Hampton plays. The Chargers were able to run the ball a lot more last week as they tripped into an early lead after the Bills' many turnovers, but it's more likely they get stuck in a trailing game script in this one. Hampton has big-play ability if he breaks into space, so taking the under on attempts might be a safer approach. I didn't want to pay the juice at under 13.5 attempts at -123 as of this posting, but if under 12.5 appears, I'll be interested in taking that. Kaleb Johnson rushing attempts OVER 8.5 (-115) The Green Bay Packers ' lack of a handoff game is harrowing. Through three games, the Packers have 146 total rushing yards from running backs -- eighth fewest for a team through three games over the past six seasons. The one-dimensionality on offense particularly haunted them against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night, but they've had a long week to explore offensive line reinforcements and recommit to the rushing attack. Green Bay has the fifth-highest pass rate over expectation per Next Gen Stats. Behind that offensive line? No shot. They need to find a rushing attack, and they know it. Critically, the Packers draw a rookie UDFA quarterback ( Jalon Daniels ) making his first career start for a bad Tampa Bay Buccaneers team. The potential to build an actual lead and salt it away should also increase the total handoffs in this game. The Packers clearly don't trust MarShawn Lloyd as a ball carrier, and Chris Brooks is the third-down back. If the running game plays a bigger role this week in a leading game script, Johnson is the most likely beneficiary. I prefer Johnson's attempts to his yardage totals, simply because the Packers' line is still a problem. But both are bettable as his role expands. Woody Marks rushing yards OVER 33.5 (-114) NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks Our Dan Graziano reported this week that his sense of the Houston Texans ' running game is that more work should go Marks' way . I'm inclined to agree. David Montgomery is a good stay-ahead-of-the-sticks rusher, but with Houston's offensive line issues, he has been unable to solve their short-yardage problems on his own. By getting the ball to Marks on the outside, the Texans can find bigger runs without worrying as much about their interior offensive line play. The Dallas Cowboys have given up 114.3 rushing yards per game to running backs through three weeks, fifth worst in the league. They have played three mobile QBs ( Jaxson Dart , Jayden Daniels , Lamar Jackson ) who make run defense more challenging, but the eye test confirms the liability of players like outside linebackers Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku in setting a hard edge. With Nico Collins back in the starting lineup for Houston, the temptation is to think the Texans will become more pass-heavy -- but their offensive philosophy this season was always to give C.J. Stroud a better running game. I'd take Marks to 36.5 this week, and I'd look at some longest rush props as well. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Zay Flowers receiving yards OVER 66.5 (-110) I had all sorts of Flowers overs to target against the Cowboys last week, but his hamstring injury limited him to just 15 routes. Of course, he still went over his yardage prop with 84 yards on only 15 routes. Flowers is a huge-play star-in-the-making in this Declan Doyle offense, and the books still haven't caught up. Flowers has now only played 1.5 games of football through three weeks, and four of those six quarters were with load management. Yet, he has 234 receiving yards and a whopping 9.36 yards per route run because of how easily the Baltimore Ravens are getting him open with motion, backfield alignment and play-action pass fakes. He's as central to this passing attack as Jaxon Smith-Njigba is to Seattle's, and as he strings together full healthy games, we'll never see a number in the 60s for him again. If you're worried about continued management on the hamstring injury, especially in a game the Ravens might dominate, consider taking Flowers' first-quarter receiving props (over 14.5 receiving yards is +100) to ensure the Ravens are still in their base offense. Michael Mayer receiving yards OVER 21.5 (-116) In Brock Bowers ' first game back healthy, Mayer's route share was totally unaffected. Mayer ran a route on 71% of the Las Vegas Raiders ' dropbacks in Week 1, 72% in Week 2, and 70% in Week 3. That's because the Raiders are using Bowers like a true wide receiver. They were in multiple-TE sets on over 80% of their total snaps, and with Bowers typically in slot or wide alignments, Mayer got the matchups against linebackers and safeties from his traditional inline alignments. Throw in the fact that the Raiders' traditional wide receivers are a thin group without much demand for targets, and I still think Mayer is the second target after Bowers. As opposing defenses spend more resources to take Bowers out of the game plan, it's Mayer who will benefit. The Raiders have a good shot of a trailing game script against the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs' run-heavy approach shortens the clock and makes it a little tougher to take receptions, so I prefer receiving yards here. But if we get into a big score deficit in the second half, I'll look for a live receptions over on Mayer. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-8 -3.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 7-4 +3.6 Receiving props 5-10 -5.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 27-29 -3.4 Walder's prop bets Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available Defensive plays Miami Dolphins to record first sack of game (+170) On one hand, this is bold because the Dolphins have not sacked the quarterback this season. Not once. On the other hand, maybe it's not that bold, because the Minnesota Vikings have taken sacks at the second-highest rate in the NFL (10.2%). Granted, that was partially with Carson Wentz in the lineup, and now Minnesota has a more mobile Kyler Murray back. But still, my belief has always been that the quarterback and offense control sacks more than the defense. I spun up a new model for this category just this week, and it seems like it agrees, considering it has the Dolphins as a plus-money value. Arizona Cardinals to NOT give up a sack on their first drive (-411) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks One of the biggest disappointments of the season thus far has been a New York Giants pass rush that has managed a 1.0% sack rate, second worst among all teams. Their pass rush win rate tells a similar story; it ranks 25th best. Now, the Cardinals' pass protection has also not been good this year, ranking second worst in pass block win rate. Despite that, they have allowed sacks on just 4.1% of dropbacks, better than the league average of 6.0%. My model believes their chances of giving up a sack on their opening drive is quite a bit lower than these odds suggest. Greg Rousseau under 0.75 sacks (+147) Rousseau is having an unbelievable start to the season, with 6.0 sacks in three games. It's a huge jump in sack pace for him: he's never recorded more than 8.0 sacks in a season. While Rousseau probably has improved, the model is skeptical he's improved as much as these odds imply. A big reason why? His pass rush win rate still isn't that great. A year ago Rousseau was in the 16th percentile in the metric at edge. Now, he's the 30th percentile. Better, sure, but it still suggests he isn't winning on a down-to-down basis as much as top-flight pass rushers. And that reduces his sack forecast going forward. I would bet this down to even money. Jermaine Johnson II over 0.25 sacks (+275) I've been a long-time Johnson skeptic, but this line has pushed the hate so far that I'm on his side now. One factor is the quarterback he's facing: Lamar Jackson . The Ravens' quarterback has taken sacks at an average-ish 5.7% clip this year, but my model isn't ready to totally forget the massive 9.8% number he recorded a year ago. And even if you don't think Johnson is great -- and I don't -- he's still on the field on 66% of the Titans' pass rushes and 77% in clear passing situations. This line is too good to pass up. I would bet this down to +175. Other sack bets I recommend: Arden Key over 0.25 sacks (+197) Abdul Carter over 0.25 sacks (+109) Dayo Odeyingbo under 0.25 sacks (-135) Jeffery Simmons over 0.25 sacks (+112) Donovan Ezeiruaku over 0.25 sacks (+249) Danielle Hunter under 0.75 sacks (-108) Andrew Van Ginkel under 0.75 sacks (-107) Leonard Williams under 0.75 sacks (-108) George Karlaftis over 0.25 sacks (+224) Aidan Hutchinson under 0.75 sacks (+131) Brandon Jones under 6.5 tackles + assists (+103) Jones is recording a tackle on 16% of opponent run plays and 8% of opponent pass plays. It's the first number that stands out, because it ranks in the 84th percentile among safeties. But here's the thing: the 49ers have been pass-heavy this season! They literally rank first in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. And every time a Broncos opponent opts to pass instead of run, that cuts Jones' chances of recording a tackle roughly in half. That's one reason why my model likes Jones' under quite a bit. I would bet this down to -132. Roquan Smith over 7.5 tackles + assists (+102) This is a low tackle line for Smith to clear, considering he's gone over 7.5 in each of his three games this season and nine out of 15 last year. On one hand, we can understand why: the Ravens are huge favorites over the Titans, and so the game script expectation is that Tennessee will fall behind and be forced to pass. For a linebacker like Smith, that would be bad for his tackling numbers since he's much more likely to record one against the run. But working in our favor is that Tennessee has been extremely run heavy thus far, ranking 31st in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Other tackle bets I recommend: Reed Blankenship under 6.5 tackles + assists (-117) Fred Warner under 8.5 tackles + assists (+104) Pat Surtain II under 4.5 tackles + assists (-102) Deommodore Lenoir under 5.5 tackles + assists (-124) Ji'Ayir Brown over 4.5 tackles + assists (-118) Offensive plays Jordan Love pass attempts UNDER 35.5 (-119) The Green Bay Packers have been pass-heavy in 2026, with the sixth-highest pass rate over expectation according to NFL Next Gen Stats. My attempts model assumes that is going to come down, because leaning that heavily on the pass game is not what the Packers have done in the past under Matt LaFleur. Green Bay ranked 26th in the same category last season. But there's also this: The Packers' offensive line has struggled immensely. I can only imagine they would want to limit the number of times Love drops back on Sunday, especially against Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles, who loves to blitz. Jaylen Wright receptions OVER 1.5 (+180) Wright and Ollie Gordon II will handle the backfield workload in the wake of De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL injury. Both have almost no experience catching the ball in the pros, but someone is going to have to catch passes out of the backfield -- and that's especially true this week. That's because the Miami Dolphins are playing the Minnesota Vikings, one of the most zone-heavy teams in the league (78% zone). Running backs catch passes against zone coverage almost twice as frequently compared to when they face man coverage, and in my back tests, betting the receptions over on running backs facing zone-heavy defenses has been profitable. Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 88587 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Follow on X Multiple Authors Nov 15, 2026, 04:21 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Wek 10 of the NFL season is already upon us. We've looked at the games, the odds and available props in hopes of trying to find the best value for bets. Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's favorite bets Solak's plays | Walder's props Clay's TD projections Bowen's favorite bets We'll start with our game pick this week with the Chiefs-Falcons matchup in Atlanta. Plus, I have multiple teasers for the Week 10 slate, and I'll add a player prop on a wide receiver who is creating explosive plays at a high rate. Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 1 p.m. ET on CBS; Line: KC -3, O/U: 46.5 Patrick Mahomes has a new target to work with as Josh Downs joins the fray against the Falcons. Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images The Chiefs added wide receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline, giving Patrick Mahomes a slot target who can create numbers after the catch. The foot quickness is there to uncover. But I like the Chiefs to cover as a road favorite because of the run game and Steve Spagnuolo's defense. Kenneth Walker III is a difference-maker in Andy Reid's offense, averaging 23.1 touches and 130.5 scrimmage yards per game. but has been ruled out for Sunday due to a groin injury, elevating rookie Emmett Johnson to the lead role. Johnson has the vision and elusive ability to find daylight versus an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 YPC (22nd in the league), while Reid can use the heavy run action to influence linebackers on play-action concepts. Defensively, Spagnuolo's unit will mix late rotation, Cover 2 and pressure against a Falcons offense that is lacking passing rhythm right now. And quarterback Michael Penix Jr . has struggled against the blitz this season (48.4 QBR). The Browns will need more rushing efficiency from Quinshon Judkins , but I feel comfortable with the altered spread at home because of a Cleveland pass defense that matches up well with Houston. In the other matchup in this teaser, Kyle Shanahan can scheme up a Dallas defense that is giving up 26.8 points and 372.7 yards per game. Look for play-action early with Brock Purdy targeting the seams and deep in-breakers, while the 49ers' defense creates issues for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game. Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-135): Minnesota Vikings +9.5 at Green Bay Packers , Buffalo Bills -2 at New York Jets The trade for Kirk Cousins should create more volume and production for Justin Jefferson , and that will open more daylight for the Vikings' run game. But I'm taking Minnesota, with the spread being bumped to +9.5 points, because of Brian Flores' defense. I expect more zone pressure here because of the vertical ability of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but the Vikings will look to create chaos for Jordan Love . I like the Bills in the other matchup. Coach Joe Brady will have pressure answers for Josh Allen to get the ball out (catch-and-run targets for DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir ), and don't be surprised if the Bills lead with a run-heavy approach to control tempo. Jameson Williams longest reception OVER 24.5 yards (-112) Williams has had a reception of 24 or more yards in five straight games. With his vertical ability, plus the dynamic open-field speed he displays after the catch, I like Williams to hit the over against New England. I love the Steelers' potential to keep this game close because they have the sort of ball-control, run-heavy offense that can minimize the number of possessions Joe Burrow gets in this game. Since Week 3, when Pittsburgh rejiggered the right side of its offensive line, the Steelers are third in success rate and first in EPA on rushing snaps; no team has a higher explosive run rate, and it isn't close. When they faced the Bengals in Week 3, Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards. Now, Rico Dowdle is back to help. The Steelers are also big on targeting the backs and tight ends in the passing game, which is where you want to go after this Bengals defense, and the lingering ankle injury to DJ Turner II also makes Cincinnati fairly weak in the secondary. It's a divisional game, and the Bengals are too hot and cold to trust with more than a field goal against a Steelers team off the bye. Rico Dowdle receiving yards OVER 13.5 (-114) Editor's Picks Joe Burrow is the NFL MVP favorite, but is he the best bet? Pamela Maldonado Early bets for NFL Week 10: Two games we're jumping on now ESPN NFL Week 10 betting odds for every game ESPN 2 Related Dowdle returned to the Steelers' lineup in Week 6 and had seven routes to Warren's 27 in that game against the Buccaneers. But he was targeted on four of those seven routes, and since then has 24 routes and six targets to Warren's 22 routes and six targets. The receiving volume has been fairly split since his return, and rightfully so -- Warren has been an exceptional between-the-tackles runner this season, and Dowdle has always been a capable pass catcher. Yet, Warren is projected for 25.5 yards and 3.5 receptions, whereas Dowdle is at 13.5 and 2.5. Given how willingly Aaron Rodgers targets the backs and how poor the Bengals' linebackers are in coverage and at tackling in the open field, backfield receiving production should be a strong part of Pittsburgh's offensive approach, and Dowdle is the far cheaper option in what should be near a 50/50 opportunity split. Keep an eye on this number live. If Warren starts out the first quarter taking most of the snaps on a couple of Pittsburgh three-and-outs, Dowdle's numbers will drop even more, and I'll start looking for live alts. Tutu Atwell receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) It's worth wondering just who it is that is going to catch passes for the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua -- who had 19 targets and 14 receptions on 43 routes last week against the Commanders -- joins Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington on the injured reserve bench. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also probably out for Sunday's game at Arizona. The two primary route runners behind Nacua at receiver last Sunday were Konata Mumpfield and Atwell, the latter of whom was targeted five times for two receptions and 16 yards. Atwell ended the day with 37 unrealized air yards -- that is to say, he had 53 air yards to the 16 receiving yards he actually produced. In back-to-back weeks, he has had at least 50 air yards on 17 and 20 routes, respectively. Given the thinness of the Rams' receiver room, 20 routes should be a floor projection for Atwell, as long as the Cardinals' offense can keep things competitive with Carson Beck under center. Even if they can't, Atwell's downfield usage can get us home on one big reception. If you're looking to get really frisky in what should be a sleepy late afternoon game, Rams rookie receiver CJ Daniels to score a touchdown is +950. He's a big-framed receiver, which the Rams will need behind the smaller Mumpfield and Atwell. Worth a sprinkle! Tre Tucker receiving yards OVER 25.5 (-115) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Speaking of unrealized air yards, Tucker is 13th among all receivers in unconnected air yards at 227. Tucker is tied for ninth in targets of at least 20 air yards but has only a 35.7% receptions rate, thanks in large part to six of those 14 targets landing inaccurate with quarterback Kirk Cousins . Cousins, for as good as he was at the helm of the Raiders' offense, lacks a deep-ball arm at this stage of his career. With rookie Fernando Mendoza ready to start his first career game, I expect the Raiders' passing attack to become less incremental and a bit more vertical, which speaks to Tucker's game. Though the matchup against the Seattle Seahawks ' defense is certainly an intimidating one for a green passer, Klint Kubiak is well suited to find space against this defense -- he saw it work for a whole season up close when he was the coordinator in Seattle last season. I'm confident he'll have a trick or two up his sleeve. I wouldn't usually take a receiving over against this Seahawks defense that leads the league in yards per target allowed to opposing wideouts. But the number is too low for a primary receiver and can be reached on one big play. I'll be on alts as well for this bet, and we also will track 40-plus yards for a half unit at +194. Geno Smith passing yards OVER 220.5 (-113) The Buffalo Bills ' defense has enjoyed two softer quarterback matchups after their bye. Against the Ravens, both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down, forcing emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano into the game. Against the Vikings, it was backup Carson Wentz . Perhaps something seriously improved in the Bills' secondary post-bye -- and they are adding safety Amani Hooker , a nice deadline addition, at safety -- but before that bye, opposing quarterbacks were ripping through Buffalo's pass defense. Cousins had 313 yards in Week 6, Matthew Stafford had 383 in Week 5, and Drake Maye had 269 in Week 4. The Bills are rightfully large favorites over the 2-7 New York Jets , who probably will run the ball early in an attempt to keep it close, then eventually get forced into a pass-heavy script. Smith has cleared this number in three of his past four games and is 11th in the league in yards per pass attempt. When the Jets have to throw, he puts up big numbers. With Garrett Wilson expected to return from the concussion protocol, the Jets' receiver trio is at full force, and Smith should produce accordingly. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Daniel Jones passing yards UNDER 186.5 (-112) The Indianapolis Colts receiver room is as bad as any I can think of in the past 10 years of non-COVID football. With Downs and Keenan Allen both traded at the deadline, the Colts are fielding Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin and Deion Burks as starting wideouts. Indianapolis retained running back Jonathan Taylor at the trade deadline, so it's fair to expect the Colts to increase their reliance on the handoff game. The Miami Dolphins ' passing defense gives up the third-most yards per pass attempt in the league but gives up only 198.4 yards per game, right around league average. That's because nobody needs to throw it against them to win. Especially with defensive tackle Zach Sieler now hurt, the Colts should be able to run the ball with plenty of success. This Colts' passing attack is as below league average as it gets, and with Malik Willis out, the likelihood the Dolphins get a second-half lead and force a pass-happy approach is greatly diminished. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-8 -3.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 7-4 +3.6 Receiving props 5-10 -5.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 27-29 -3.4 Walder's prop bets Defensive plays Indianapolis Colts D/ST Anytime TD (+550) This is straightforward: We're trying to capitalize on Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord making his NFL debut. Is the Colts' defense good? It is not. But it almost doesn't matter. Indianapolis is a 3.5-point favorite, and the chances of a disastrous mistake from McCord is elevated given his status as a former sixth-round pick who has never taken a pro snap in a regular-season game. My model, which is making those quite negative assumptions about McCord, prices this at +450. New England Patriots to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-391) The Patriots are light underdogs this week against the Detroit Lions , who do boast the second-best pass rush win rate this season. But the Patriots are third best in pass block win rate, which, along with Drake Maye 's average sack rate, is why my model isn't overly concerned about Maye falling to a first-drive sack. At least not at this price, anyway. I make the fair line -514. Chase Young under 0.75 sacks (+158) Believe it or not Young is tied for second in the NFL in sacks with 8.0 (only behind Will Anderson Jr .) and this line is absolutely a reflection of that. I generally consider myself a Chase Young backer -- because after the early disappointment of his career he quickly became underrated - but wow has this gone too far. In fact, if the line closes at this price it would be the strongest sack prop line of the year. There is no way Young - whose pass rush win rate is above average but still just in the 69th percentile - is on that kind of level. Chop Robinson over 0.25 sacks (+132) This will be the fifth time I've bet Robinson's sack over in this year's column and it doesn't look like we'll be slowing down any time soon (we're 2-2 and +1.1 units thus far). Robinson is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. Let me say that again: he is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. And to back it up: he leads edge rushers in pressure rate, too! That's multiple forms of measurement coming away with the same conclusion: on a down-to-down basis Robinson is consistently beating his blocker and causing problems for the quarterback. That it's only resulted in 4.0 sacks is why we still get to bet it at this price. And this week, we get an added bonus: the Dolphins aren't even that big underdogs this week (+4.5 at the Colts). Other sack bets I recommend: Gabe Jacas under 0.25 sacks (-200) Josh Uche over 0.25 sacks (+209) Andrew Van Ginkel under 0.75 sacks (-107) Maliek Collins under 0.25 sacks (-181) Chris Jones under 0.25 sacks (-176) Josh Sweat over 0.25 sacks (+184) Maxx Crosby over 0.25 sacks (+115) Byron Murphy II under 0.25 sacks (-204) Quinnen Williams under 0.25 sacks (-192) Nick Bosa under 0.25 sacks (-154) Dexter Lawrence II under 0.25 sacks (-218) Grover Stewart under 3.5 tackles + assists (-111) Stewart used to be one of the very best run-stuffers among nose tackles. Two years ago he recorded a tackle rate on run plays that ranked in the 94th percentile among interior linemen with at least 300 snaps played, along with a 97th percentile run stop win rate. But he is not the same player now at age 33. Among defensive tackles with 200 snaps plays this year Stewart ranks in the 63rd percentile in tackle rate against the run and the 12th percentile in run stop win rate. Even against the run-heavy Dolphins my model believes this line is a little too optimistic for Stewart. Bryan Cook under 6.5 tackles + assists (-149) This is an increased line from where Cook has been in the past couple of weeks after he went over this number twice in the last three games (though those are the only two times he's gone over this line all year). Only 29% of tackle lines on safeties this year have been 6.5 or higher, and I'm not sure Cook ought to be quite on that level even with this number shaded under. Cook ranks in the 82nd percentile in tackle rate vs. the pass but just 38th percentile against the run, but those equate to nearly equal tackling rates so I don't think game script is a huge factor here. Overall, my model thinks this line is a little high. Other tackle bets I recommend: Dane Belton under 7.5 tackles + assists ( +115) Christian Gonzalez under 4.5 tackles + assists (-116) College Football Playoff Bracket Challenge Fill out up to TWO College Football Playoff brackets! Create a Bracket Offensive plays Chase Brown receptions OVER 4.5 (+102) Almost every week, I have a bet based on one of my favorite splits in football: running back reception rates against man vs. zone coverage. Running backs record a reception on 8% dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone. And based on back-testing research, I don't believe this fact is fully baked into reception lines. The last couple of weeks I've used this information to bet the under on running backs facing man-heavy defenses -- we hit on Alvin Kamara 's under last week -- but this time I'm flipping the script and opting for Brown's over against the Steelers. Pittsburgh is the heaviest zone coverage team in the NFL, running zone 79% of the time. Malik Washington receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-116) Washington has a huge split between his open score (82, T2) and his catch score (38, below average). Those are two player tracking-based metrics from ESPN Analytics, with the former measuring a receiver's ability to get open (regardless of target) on every route and the latter measuring their ability to make the catch relative to expectations. Open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates more strongly with production, so Washington fits the exact profile of receiver I want to bet on. Yes, he will have McCord throwing to him. But I also think this is a particularly good matchup; Colts nickel corner Justin Walley has been out, but even if he returns, he has had a rough season, giving up 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's much higher than average. This bet is based on my read of the number above and not an output from a model, the way most of my bets are. articles.description: Will Hill is back with his best bet for every NFL Week 4 game.
articles.text: 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers | FOX Sports my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores Watch Betting Stories Search Sign In Account SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS POPULAR SEARCHES - No Data Available - BROWSE BY SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS Built on National Football League National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers Published Oct. 1, 2026 1:55 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Will Hill FOX Sports Betting Analyst There are several barnburners on tap for NFL Week 4. Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. Sign up Odds by Videos Columns Leagues MLB NFL NBA College Football College Basketball MLB NFL NBA College Football College Basketball Odds NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Premier League WNBA NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Premier League WNBA 2026 NFL Week 10 Best Bets, Picks, Predictions, Player Props, Odds: Lions vs Patriots, Steelers vs Bengals By Vaughn Dalzell , By Vaughn Dalzell Published November 12, 2026 11:31 PM Add on Google Facebook Twitter Email Add on Google Week 10 started with a thriller on Thursday Night Football between the Commanders and Giants! After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. Jacksonville ranks fifth in the NFL with 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game, but that also dropped after Justice Hill had a garbage-time 65-yard run last week. Pollard has hit the over in three straight games and is 5-3 to the over on the season. I’m buying into regression hitting this week. I’m taking the under 58.5 rushing yards down to 53.5. I expect a negative game script and Pollard’s role in the pass game to increase here, and his carries regress back to the norm. Last season, Pollard ran for 60 and 48 yards against the Jaguars on 10 and 14 carries. Jacksonville won by 22 and 34 points. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 58.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Vikings at Packers (-3): O/U 42.5 Did you know that Jordan Love is the only quarterback to throw for two touchdowns against the Vikings this season? That was in Week 1, so seven-straight quarterbacks have thrown for one or fewer touchdowns against Minnesota. Well, fast forward to Week 10, and Green Bay still doesn’t have a running game, so Love has carried the offense. If the Packers are to score more than two touchdowns in this game, it’s hard for me to see it not coming from the arm of Love. He is 8-1 to the over 1.5 passing touchdowns this season. I’ll take him to go Over 1.5 passing touchdowns against Minnesota again and ride his heater of three-straight overs. Outside boundary receivers have had a hard time against Minnesota this season, but one wideout that burned the Vikings defense was Matthew Golden . He’s burned me too. I faded Golden the past two weeks, and he snuck over with 79 yards, then had a monster 164 yards against New England. This becomes a fade spot of a career-high and after catching all 10 targets. I am going under 71.5 yards on Golden, down to 66.5. I’ll root for a red zone touchdown from him, though. Picks: Jordan Love Over 1.5 Passing TDs (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 71.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Steelers at Bengals (-3.5): O/U 49.5 It may be November, but this game will feel like a December or January clash with playoff implications. The Steelers and Bengals are both on four-game winning streaks, and the winner will be in first place in the AFC North. The spread and total for this first game were Bengals -3.5 and 42.5, so we have a full seven-point correction on the total for the second game after Pittsburgh won 30-27 in Week 3. Pittsburgh has been money in years past with Mike Tomlin coming off a bye week (17-5 ML), but this Mike McCarthy’s team now, plus the Bengals, are incredible when at a rest disadvantage. Since 2019 with Zac Taylor , the Bengals are 18-5-1 ATS with a rest disadvantage. Rather than picking a side, I am going under 24.5 points in the first half. The first-half score was 17-17 in Week 3 and flew over the 20.5 first-half total. There could be a lack of rhythm early coming out of the break for the Steelers, and it’ll be hard for the Bengals to replicate or improve on their 7.1-yard play last week against Atlanta. Plus, the Bengals are going off an overseas game, which is never easy on the body. With the intensity of this game early, I like the first half under 24.5 points. Neither team has played anybody good while lighting it up during their four-game win streaks, so the defenses may surprise us. Pick: Steelers vs Bengals 1H Under 24.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! This is as good of a matchup for the Chargers offense as it gets. Baltimore has allowed 33-plus points in three straight games, and it might not get better with questionable tags to three starting defensive backs. This is also the Chargers’ first primetime game of the season and first of two or three (Week 15 could get flexed). I think Los Angeles will want this game a little more, and Jim Harbaugh might call up his brother John for any secrets to pull off the win against his former Ravens team. It doesn’t scare me that Jacoby Brissett will be making his Ravens debut in Baltimore on Monday Night Football, because, like I said, that Ravens’ defense has some serious issues. The Chargers finally found the end zone last week after 37 straight drives without a touchdown, and I think they’ll find it more than once in Baltimore. I like the Chargers to get the first cover of the season (0-7-1 ATS), and I think they can win too. Baltimore is 0-4 ATS at home (worst) and 2-7 ATS this season (third-worst). I will take L.A. +4.5. Betting “against the spread” refers to the act of choosing the winning team based on a numeric handicap placed on the team that oddsmakers believe is superior, rather than picking the outright winner. For example, if the Rams face the Bengals, and oddsmakers set the spread at Rams -3.5, you would need Los Angeles to win by 4 or more points in order to cash your Rams bet. What is an Over/Under Bet? Over/Under is a wager based on how many points you think will be scored in a specific game. Oddsmakers set the total, and bettors decide whether the final score will be higher or lower than that number. If an Over/Under is set at 44.5 points and you bet Over, you will need the combined score of both teams to be 45 points or higher to win your bet. What is a Moneyline Bet? A moneyline bet involves choosing which team you believe will win a specific matchup. The moneyline favorite carries a minus designation, like -130. This means that you need to wager $130 to earn a $100 profit. Conversely, the underdog carries a plus designation, like +110. This means that you win $110 in profit on a $100 bet. Please include the odds with your selection. Rueben Bain Jr. to be a Top 10 pick: Yes ( -162 ) “Miami Hurricanes EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. has 30.9-inch arms, which likely cause him to slide, but I don't think he can get past eight overall to the New Orleans Saints or nine overall to the Kansas City Chiefs. The 21-year-old finished fifth in the ACC with 7.5 sacks as a freshman, before regressing somewhat as a sophomore while battling injuries. Bain Jr. then returned to form this past year, setting career-highs in tackles (54), tackles for loss (15.5), and sacks (9.5), while leading the Hurricanes to a College Football Playoff (CFP) National Championship appearance. This earned him AP Consensus All-America and ACC Defensive Player of the Year honors, as well as the Ted Hendricks Award. Those accomplishments, a high character, and elite film should be enough to keep him inside the top 10 picks, making this arguably the best prop bet available.” – Seth Woolcock ( FantasyPros ) Jacob Rodriguez drafted inside the top-32 ( +500 ) “I’m a sucker for the “Will this player be drafted in Round 1″ betting market. Right now, my favorite approach is to select Texas Tech LB Jacob Rodriguez inside the top-32 at 5-1 odds. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Jermod McCoy (Tennessee), Colton Hood (Tennessee), and Ty Simpson (Alabama) are better than 50/50 to go in the first round, but McCoy’s stock is plummeting due to a worrisome knee issue, and there are only two or three potential first-round suitors for Simpson, none of whom would draft him with the picks they currently hold in the top half of the round. If all of these SEC maybes make it, that’s seven, leaving one SEC player to spare. Chase Bisontis (Texas A&M), Cashius Howell (Texas A&M), Zion Young (Missouri), C.J. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile. While Jordyn Tyson is hands down the best pure receiver in this class, his extensive injury history, including major knee surgery and a broken collarbone, has dropped him to the second or third receiver off the board on most teams’ lists. NFL front offices are notoriously risk-averse in the top ten, making Tate the safer bet to anchor a professional offense immediately. This shift in draft stock highlights a classic case where reliability outweighs elite but fragile potential. Ultimately, taking Tate at these odds is a play on the certainty of his health and polished Buckeye pedigree over the medical gamble Tyson presents.” – Lawrence Iacona ( Gridiron Experts ) Makai Lemon to be first WR drafted ( +2000 ) “Makai Lemon – 1st Wide Receiver Drafted ( +2000 at Caesars ). I'm going with Makai Lemon as the first wide receiver off the board. Bold, absolutely. Crazy? Maybe, but hear me out. This is often a copycat league. I believe a wide receiver-needy team, such as the New York Giants, might consider Lemon. The Giants already have Malik Nabers, a top outside threat, and could look to replicate what Seattle did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit with Amon-Ra St. Brown, using Lemon in a similar role. I'm going with the Giants selecting Lemon at 5, assuming Jeremiyah Love is already off the board.” – Paul Brenton ( EPB1983Dynasty ) Related articles Best Bucks vs. Heat NBA Props & Picks (Wednesday) Best Celtics vs. Nuggets NBA Props & Picks (Wednesday) NBA Picks & Predictions: Wednesday (11/18) College Football Picks & Predictions: Week 12 (Wednesday) College Football Picks & Predictions: Week 12 (Tuesday) NBA Picks & Predictions: Tuesday (11/17) Click to go to homepage NFL Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards NBA Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards NCAAF Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Leaderboards Articles Teams Podcast Careers Product Updates BettingPros API Get Involved About Us Contact Us Terms of Use Privacy Policy Third Party Licenses Do Not Sell Accessibility Disclosures Affiliate Signup © 2018–2026 BettingPros.com. If you'd rather watch than read, start with this PrizePicks Optimizer tutorial . What is the PrizePicks Optimizer? PrizePicks hides the odds inside payout multipliers. The BettingPros PrizePicks Optimizer turns those multipliers into real per-pick odds, puts you in the slip structure with the best expected return, and grades every prop against sportsbook and prediction-market consensus. Why slip size comes first Before you pick a single player, the size of your slip has already set your odds. A 2-pick Power Play prices around -137 — both legs have to hit, and you need roughly 58% per leg just to break even. A 5-pick Flex Play prices closer to -119, pays 10x when you go 5-for-5 and 2x when you go 4-for-5, and drops the break-even rate to about 54% per leg. The 6-pick Flex sits in the same neighborhood at about -118. The 2-pick feels safer. The Flex is the better price. The Optimizer defaults to the 5-pick Flex for a reason. PrizePicks can tweak payouts by promo and by state, so check the numbers on your board. The structure holds either way: Flex trades a lower ceiling for a lower bar, and the lower bar is what pays you back over time. How to read the board Every prop is ranked against market consensus: sharp sportsbooks and prediction markets, not a gut call or lock of the week. Green means the pick clears the break-even rate for the slip size you selected. Red means it doesn't. Change the slip size and the colors will move with it to match the updated requirements. Demons, goblins, and juiced lines are stripped out, so you're only looking at clean, unadjusted numbers. Build from the green, even when a red prop is a player you love. Win rate is the wrong scoreboard Treat each leg as its own bet. If every leg is +EV, the slip is +EV. You can cash 42% of your slips and finish ahead if the prices are right, or win more than half and still lose money paying juiced odds. The Optimizer won't make every slip a winner, but it puts you on the side of the math that can actually be beaten over time with volume. Same effort either way. Only one of those versions wins over time. What makes a good prop pick? The best PrizePicks slips pair a clear projection edge with a realistic win rate. On a Power Play every pick must hit, so favor picks where our projection clears the line comfortably and recent form agrees; on a Flex Play you can absorb a miss, so a little more variance is acceptable in exchange for upside. Avoid loading a slip with correlated props from the same game — one quiet night can take down several legs at once. Spread picks across games and sports, and use the expected-value column to break ties between picks with similar win probabilities.
