Demons, goblins, and juiced lines are stripped out, so you're only looking at clean, unadjusted numbers. Build from the green, even when a red prop is a player you love. Win rate is the wrong scoreboard Treat each leg as its own bet. If every leg is +EV, the slip is +EV. You can cash 42% of your slips and finish ahead if the prices are right, or win more than half and still lose money paying juiced odds. The Optimizer won't make every slip a winner, but it puts you on the side of the math that can actually be beaten over time with volume. Same effort either way. Only one of those versions wins over time. What makes a good prop pick? The best PrizePicks slips pair a clear projection edge with a realistic win rate.

The Big Game has become a full menu of prop markets that attract both casual fans and seasoned bettors. From the opening coin toss to the l ength of the national anthem , and even the color of the post-game Gatorade shower , novelty wagers have become a major part of the experience and consistently draw heavy interest leading up to kickoff. Below, we break down some of the most popular Super Bowl props along with how they've performed historically, also providing some of our expert's predictions on whether the Seattle Seahawks or New England Patriots will lift the Lombardi Trophy. All odds below were taken from FanDuel Sportsbook as of Feb. 7. Let's take a look: Super Bowl LX odds Seahawks vs. Patriots Spread: Seahawks -4.5 Moneyline: Seahawks -235, Patriots +194 O/U: 45.5 Super Bowl LX MVP odds Sam Darnold : +115 (bet $10 to win $21.50 total) Drake Maye : +230 (bet $10 to win $33 total) Jaxon Smith-Njigba : +550 (bet $10 to win $65 total) Kenneth Walker III : +850 (bet $10 to win $95 total) Rhamondre Stevenson : +3000 (bet $10 to win $410 total) Rashid Shaheed : +3000 (bet $10 to win $310 total) Stefon Diggs : +4000 (bet $10 to win $410 total) This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Expert Predictions Will Hill : Seahawks 27, Patriots 17 The Patriots have had a remarkable turnaround post-Bill Belichick, but the Seahawks will pose a significant step-up in competition compared to what the AFC bracket presented. I expect a low-scoring game, but I think the more talented Seahawks will ultimately pull away and win 27-17, with Sam Darnold taking home MVP. Chris Fallica : Seahawks 27, Patriots 23 I hate the game from a spread standpoint. It seems like a simple handicap where Seattle is better at every position group, and groupthink has the Seahawks winning comfortably. If anything, I’ll see if I can get a cheap Seahawks moneyline on the game, but I’m not going to lay 4.5 here. Sammy P : Seahawks 23, Patriots 20 After a low-scoring first quarter, I expect things to stay competitive the rest of the way. New England (15-5 ATS) made bettors money all season long and that mostly came in the favorite role. Mike Vrabel is a tremendous underdog coach and that song should remain the same this Sunday in Santa Clara. Geoff Schwartz : Seahawks 24, Patriots 13 I have the game 24-13 for the Seahawks. The Seahawks have been the best team wire-to-wire this season and the best case for the Patriots in this game is Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold turning back into a pumpkin, which I don't expect. He's been nails this postseason. The Seattle defense is going to sit in zone coverage and force New England to work for all its yards, which is difficult without dynamic playmakers at the skill positions. The Seahawks win this game comfortably. National Anthem For years, sports fans have bet on the length of the Star Spangled Banner, among other anthem-related props. And there will be some added intrigue when the Seahawks offense and Bears defense are on the field, after each team just made major acquisitions. The Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts and the Bears dished out two first-round picks to add Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans . These two former AFC South foes will draw the spotlight when these units square off, and whoever has the better debut could help decide who wins this game. I tend to agree, for what I am guessing is the same reason that FPI likes Chicago relative to the spread: offense is more stable than defense. A good offense is simply more likely to have a strong next game than an equivalently good defense is. And if we isolate the Bears offense to just when Williams is on the field, the Bears offense and Seahawks defense do appear roughly equivalent. Plus, Sam Darnold has struggled this season and entered Sunday ranked 23rd in QBR. Give me the Bears +3 . That one pick came against the Minnesota Vikings in a monsoon. The Seahawks don't need inclement weather or heavy blitz packages to tally takeaways, though. Instead, Mike Macdonald generates pressure via stunts and disguises. His methods have clearly worked, as Seattle ranks second in the NFL in takeaways with eight. Williams is still learning, and given his desire to push -- particularly on primetime -- increases the odds of at least one ill-timed toss downfield. NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. Player A — Over 45.5 receiving yards (-115) — 53.5% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $187 return Player B — Over 45.5 receiving yards (+105) — 48.8% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $205 return When Do NFL Player Props Come Out Each Week? Some marquee player props are posted earlier in the week, but the majority are released on Wednesday or Thursday after injury reports have been announced. Follow on X Multiple Authors Sep 25, 2026, 06:39 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins (-10.5, 46.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Fla. Travis Kelce is off to a fast start for the Chiefs, who are big favorites Sunday in Miami. Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites). That can be bad business given the talent level and coaching we get on Sundays. But looking at the matchup and scheme advantages with Kansas City, I'm in on Andy Reid's team. I'll give you my quick notes for both clubs, along with some player props. NFL betting • Best bets for Sunday: Cincy in danger? • Burrow passes Allen as MVP fave | Odds • Why Lawrence is the best MVP value • Betting favorites go 14-1 in Week 9 • Odds for Week 10 games | Early bets • Super Bowl odds: Jaguars move up • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Chiefs have the ball: The offseason addition of Kenneth Walker III has given the Chiefs a true difference-maker with dual-threat traits in the backfield. Walker has rushed for at least 117 yards -- with at least 23 carries -- in both games this season, and in a Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts he caught six of 10 targets for 61 yards. We can expect Walker to get his touches on the ground against a Miami defense giving up 112.5 rushing yards per game (18th in the NFL), which allows Reid's unit to control offensive tempo. In the pass game, I see clear matchup advantages for the Chiefs. The Dolphins are giving up an average of 8.6 YPA (30th in the NFL), and they play man coverage at a rate of 58.9% (fourth most). Look for Reid to set up his receivers for catch-and-run throws from Patrick Mahomes , with Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce working multiple levels of the field against a Miami secondary that lacks high-end talent. When Miami has the ball: The Dolphins have struggled to build offensive rhythm and lack an identity, having failed to score more than 13 points in each of their first two games. Running back De'Von Achane has rushed for a total of 110 yards this season, and we aren't seeing his elite pass-catching ability (he has only 49 yards receiving). Quarterback Malik Willis has shown flashes, but his accuracy has been inconsistent (completing 58% of his passes), and he has thrown only one touchdown pass. Now, Miami does have some young talent in the pass game with Malik Washington , Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , but Douglas has been ruled out for this matchup after missing practice all week with an ankle injury. The Dolphins lack a proven No. 1 who can win critical game situations at a high rate and they average only 183.5 passing yards per game. Now they'll face a multiple Chiefs defense -- one that leans on late movement and schemed pressure. This Kansas City defense is giving up 90 yards rushing per game and only 5.5 YPA. Miami will need to find a way to create positive game flow while producing some explosive plays to stay in this one. NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Now, let's get to some prop bets ... Rashee Rice receiving yards OVER 47.5 (-114) Rice, who caught four of six targets for 83 yards in the Week 2 win over the Colts, could have early opportunities against the Dolphins' single-high man coverages. Rice can turn an underneath throw into an explosive gain. Travis Kelce receptions OVER 4.5 receptions (-114) Kelce's play speed looked different last week against the Colts, both in the route stem and after the catch. Kelce caught nine of 11 targets in that game, using his high-end coverage awareness to find open grass. He should be a priority target again for Mahomes on Sunday. Tyquan Thornton anytime TD (+475) I'm thinking of a shot-play throw here to Thornton on Sunday. Thornton caught all four of his targets for 86 yards last week against the Colts, so look for Reid to set up him on a deep-ball concept in Miami. Not one of WR Zay Flowers , OT Ronnie Stanley or OLB Trey Hendrickson practiced Wednesday for the Ravens. Still, head coach Jesse Minter said after practice that he feels "like we will have a good shot with a lot of guys this week." Editor's Picks Top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 3 Mike Clay NFL Week 3 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game NFL awards: Burrow odds-on favorite for MVP, Gibbs and JSN in tight race for OPOY Doug Greenberg 2 Related Assuming the Ravens are relatively close to full strength, I like their matchup against Dallas quite a bit. The Cowboys' back seven has struggled tremendously through two weeks of the Christian Parker era on defense; it's a challenging defensive scheme, and they are generally lacking for team speed. Their light edge rushers can be targeted in the run game. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has excelled at two things so far: attacking the edge in the running game, and generating YAC opportunities for Flowers. Baltimore might steamroll the Cowboys. I'm a little worried about the travel and field in Brazil, which can introduce some chaos. The Cowboys' offense can also score in bunches. But the Ravens are a better pressure team, thanks to the play of Hendrickson and Minter's willingness to send pressures on key downs. I like them to get enough stops in what should be a high-scoring affair. I'd take this up to -4 (-110), but only if we get positive injury news throughout the week. Houston Texans -1.5 (-118) at Indianapolis Colts Two 0-2 division rivals seemingly with their seasons already on the line -- intense stuff for Week 3. I admired the Colts' pluck in their game against the Chiefs, but the Texans' defense is made of far stiffer stuff. Houston has won the last five games between the teams, though QB Daniel Jones was hurt for the most recent matchup. NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks The Colts have relied heavily on big-play receiver Alec Pierce to generate explosive plays against DeMeco Ryans' aggressive defense. Last season against the Texans across two games, Pierce had eight catches, 210 yards and three touchdowns. Pierce hurt his heel against the Chiefs and is on injured reserve, which puts all the more pressure on Josh Downs , Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell at receiver. It's hard to imagine the Colts finding the same big plays that the Buffalo Bills and Cincinnati Bengals have against this Texans secondary. It looks like star receiver Nico Collins will miss another week with a hamstring injury, which has pulled this line down to -1.5 after opening at -2.5 and flirting with -3 throughout the week. I'm still on the Texans' side here -- their offense moved the ball much better against Cincinnati defense than the scoreboard would indicate (35.1% success rate was far better than the Bengals' 27.6% on the day). The Colts' linebacker room is such a liability that I expect C.J. Stroud to still have a strong day working the middle of the field. David Montgomery anytime TD (-110), 2+ TD scorer (+550) I'm thrilled to get Montgomery back down near even money after the Texans' absolute stinker against the Bengals in Week 2. Montgomery's number is low this week out of fear of another inept offensive day without Collins, but the Texans weren't all that bad on offense. One drive ended at the Bengals' 16-yard line on a fumbled field goal try. Another ended on the Bengals' 18 on a fourth-and-1 run failure. Another resulted in a field goal from the Bengals' 19, a fearful attempt on fourth-and-1 as the Bengals were dominating in short yardage. So, the Texans moved the ball a lot more effectively than the scoreboard would indicate. They'll be much better in short yardage when they don't have DT Dexter Lawrence II to face -- and, in general, they should find easier offense against a young and leaky Colts defense. We already know that once the Texans are in the red zone, they mash the Montgomery button aggressively -- doubly so, I'd imagine, if Collins can't go. I have a unit on 1+ touchdown and a quarter-unit on two touchdowns at +550, which I wouldn't take any lower than +530. Trey McBride and the Cardinals' offense could pose some matchup problems for the 49ers. Gary A. Vasquez/Imagn Images Arizona Cardinals +8.5 (-112) at San Francisco 49ers These are two teams about which, I'd argue, we still know very little. The 49ers got the sleepy Los Angeles Rams in Week 1 Down Under and trounced them thoroughly. They drew the listless Dolphins in Week 2 and gave them the business as well. I have no doubt the 49ers are a good team, but how good is unclear -- and they've gotten even more banged up in the interim. DT C.J. West is going on injured reserve, and WR Demarcus Robinson is expected to sit out time because of a high-ankle sprain. Behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr ., the 49ers are perilously thin at wide receiver. Of course, the Cardinals have their own injuries at corner ( Will Johnson , Max Melton , Garrett Williams ), but they're a heavy zone team anyway and can hide those issues more easily. The Cardinals got the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, and that win looked good ... until we saw the Chargers in Week 2. Arizona's offense got punked by Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks defense, but I've seen elite offenses struggle against that group. I still suspect this is a perfectly average offense, and the 49ers' defense is still a suspiciously young and thin group. I think the Cardinals get a good ground game going that shortens this contest and keeps it within a touchdown. Even if the 49ers get an early lead, I don't think they have a great answer for TE Trey McBride . If they pull LB Fred Warner out of the middle of the field to stick with the tight end in man coverage, Jacoby Brissett and Mike LaFleur will start spamming in-breakers. I'd take this to +8. Emmett Johnson rushing + receiving yards OVER 38.5 (-114) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks Johnson, a fifth-round rookie running back out of Nebraska, is the clear RB2 behind Kenneth Walker III, and he has been explosive in limited usage (39 yards on 10 carries and 64 yards on four receptions). He's an aggressive, upfield runner who seeks contact and sheds it well -- and, because he can contribute on both running and receiving downs, he's a good foil to Walker. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites over the Dolphins in Miami this Sunday, and in a blowout script, we can anticipate Johnson gets a heavy dose of running game usage. He has been more effective as a dump-off player, so I like taking his rushing and receiving yards here as a protection against game script and overall efficiency. If he runs into loaded boxes in a lopsided second half and doesn't accumulate yardage, or if the game ends up oddly close, he still can pop a big reception against the passive Dolphins defense and still get home. I would take this line up to 40 yards, and I'd consider overs on rushing attempts as well when that posts. KC Concepcion receiving yards OVER 32.5 (-112) I'm back to the well on Concepcion, who burned us last week with only 29 yards on six receptions. The Cleveland Browns had a couple of downfield plays dialed up for Concepcion, whom they continued to use in enticing ways from the slot and in motion, but they never got the ball in the air. Still, we have a player getting designed touches in the screen game and who is the safety valve underneath and is also still running vertical routes, with an average route depth (12.4) just below the league average for WRs (13.0). I see no reason to fade Concepcion's route totals, especially against a Carolina Panthers defense that has faced only one real offense so far this year (and gave up 59 points when they did so). The Browns are also always liable to enter a big negative game script, which should funnel easy targets. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. Concepcion will get home this week. I'd take the number up to 34.5. Bo Nix rushing yards UNDER 17.5 (-111) Your League, Your Rules Create a league and customize league size, scoring and rules to play in the league you want to play in. Create a league today! There has been only one scramble through two games for Nix in 2026, which is notable, as Nix was scrambling 2.3 times per game in 2025. It doesn't seem to be related to the ankle injury -- he's moving just fine -- so my theory is that it's related to the new Davis Webb offensive approach. Either the Broncos brass has stressed upon him the importance of putting the ball in play, or Nix is more comfortable with the playcalls as they're given to him and is less likely to cut bait to tuck and go. Whatever it is, I'll take his under on his rushing yards against the Rams. With the litany of RB injuries the Broncos have, I think the Rams will be willing to play Nix's keeps on read-option a little more aggressively. I also expect the Rams to be a heavy zone team in this game despite the shift to man coverage in Week 2. Nix has historically been a much shakier passer against zone than man coverage. Zone coverage allows defenders to keep their eyes on scrambling quarterbacks, which limits yardage on the hoof. I wouldn't take the number any lower than this -- just one big run could get us in trouble at such a small figure. Geno Smith 2+ passing TDs (+157) There's huge familiarity here between Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell and New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, who was Campbell's defensive coordinator in Detroit for three seasons. Glenn's linebackers coach, Kelvin Sheppard, has replaced him and runs a similar, but slightly more versatile defense. Still, I expect Glenn to have a good bead on the things that will give Sheppard trouble, especially in spots where coverage gets predictable -- like the red zone. Detroit's defense plays with heavier boxes than any defense in football, so I expect a lot of dropbacks for Smith. With Mason Taylor out because of a wrist injury, the Jets have also lost their primary in-line tight end, and I think the rushing efficiency is going to suffer. Of all the Smith overs I'm interested in this week, I'll take 2+ passing touchdowns at this long of a number. Smith has thrown only one TD pass, but the Jets are 53.3% pass in the red zone through two games (right around league average). They aren't hiding him at this part of the field. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-8 -3.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 7-4 +3.6 Receiving props 5-10 -5.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 27-29 -3.4 Walder's prop bets Kyler Murray will make his return Sunday after recovering from a concussion sustained in Week 1. Jeffrey Becker/Imagn Images Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available Defensive plays Chargers to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-311) Everything is bad with the Chargers. But it's not this bad. For context, the same bet for the Bills is -482. Even the Commanders, similarly-sized underdogs with a backup quarterback going against an elite Seattle defense, are -349 this week. So, at -311, I see the Chargers as a value. And though the Chargers being big underdogs increases the chance of Justin Herbert getting sacked during the game, that effect is mitigated early on. The Chargers won't be forced into a desperate must-pass situation on their first drive. Plus, the Bills rank just 27th in pass rush win rate, which further lowers the probability of a first-drive sack. Derrick Brown UNDER 0.25 sacks (-140) The first sack bet I listed in this column all year was betting against Deshaun Watson and his incredibly high sack rate. He has continued taking sacks at an incredible clip ... on 11.9% of his dropbacks this season. So why bet under? Because for every bet there's a price where it makes sense. And -140 is a price where I'm willing to fade Brown, even in a tantalizing matchup against Cleveland and Watson. Brown is a good player but taking down the quarterback is not his primary skill: he has just 13.0 sacks in his career. And he's actually rushing the passer a little less frequently this season than last year. I would bet this all the way down to -210. A'Shawn Robinson UNDER 0.25 sacks (-388) This might be the least fun bet recommended in this column all year. But value is value! And I'll bet it at all any part along the odds spectrum. Robinson has just 16.0 sacks since he entered the league in 2016, and I think he's particularly unlikely to get No. 17 in this game. That's because of when he's playing. The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career. If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150. Offensive plays Kyler Murray interceptions UNDER 0.5 (+121) The thing to know about forecasting interceptions is how close to 50/50 the baseline expectation for the average quarterback in the average game is. So when we see a +121 line for the under, that usually indicates a poor quarterback and/or a heavy underdog. I don't think Murray is that. Whatever you think of Murray -- and, I'll admit, I've long been a little more bullish on him than consensus -- he has been very consistent in terms of his interception rate, ranging between 1.6% and 1.8% each of his four previous seasons, all at or a little better than average. During that span, he never had a dropped interception, either. Add in that the Minnesota Vikings are favored and my model doesn't see why Murray should to be priced this way. I would bet this down to +105. Bryce Young pass attempts UNDER 33.5 (-124) The Carolina Panthers have been surprisingly pass-happy through the first two weeks of the season, with a plus-4% pass rate over expectation, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, fifth highest in the NFL. That's a massive departure from last year, when Carolina was negative 8% and ranked 31st in the same category. This bet hinges on whether what we've seen thus far continues. My attempts model is betting not. And there's also another quite simple path to a win here: If the Panthers simply blow out the Browns early -- and that's always possible when you're facing Deshaun Watson -- they'll rely on the run game in the second half. He has responded with 69 yards in the last two games. Williams has caught every target thrown his way, showing his reliability. With most coverage focused on Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, Williams should find some open looks downfield. He has cleared 30+ yards in each game this season, so 25+ yards seems reasonable at almost even money. Follow on X Multiple Authors Oct 10, 2026, 11:57 PM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 5. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, the top game to bet, favorite defensive props to play and the top predicted TD scorers. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week Solak's plays | Walder's props Clay's TD projections Bowen's Game of the Week Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 44.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh Aaron Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three TDs last week, and Jaylen Warren had 126 total yards. Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images We need to have a bounce-back week here after betting on the Bills last Sunday. So, let's pivot to a rested Pittsburgh team that played Thursday night in Week 4 at home against an Indianapolis team straight off a London trip. We'll look at both sides of the ball, then hit some props from this game and across the league in Week 5. NFL betting • Best bets for Sunday: Cincy in danger? • Burrow passes Allen as MVP fave | Odds • Why Lawrence is the best MVP value • Betting favorites go 14-1 in Week 9 • Odds for Week 10 games | Early bets • Super Bowl odds: Jaguars move up • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Steelers have the ball: Running back Jaylen Warren has seen his usage (and production) elevate over the past two games. During this stretch (against Cincinnati and Cleveland) Warren has averaged 6.5 yards per carry, 21 touches and 151 scrimmage yards. He's also playing fast on the tape, and there's a lot of outside zone here, with Warren finding daylight. Plus, he's getting the ball on swings, screens and checkdowns. This is a good matchup for Warren against a Colts defense giving up 131 rushing yards per game (28th in the league). I expect a volume day for the Steelers' lead back. The Colts' defensive numbers in the pass game point to a Pittsburgh edge as well, as the Colts are giving up 261.3 yards per game through the air and are pressuring the QB at a rate of only 28.3% (29th in the league). But can the Steelers protect and give Aaron Rodgers time and a clean pocket? Rodgers has three touchdown passes and six completions of 15 or more air yards in each of his past two games, but he has been sacked seven times during that stretch and a total of 13 times on the season (tied for most in the league). Rodgers' declining mobility also plays a role, but he needs the pocket to throw vertically to DK Metcalf and work the play-action pass game in Mike McCarthy's offense. When the Colts have the ball: This offense runs through Jonathan Taylor . The Colts' running back ranks fifth in the NFL at 88.3 rushing yards per game, and his 86 carries are the third most through four games. He's a volume back with home run ability. Taylor has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season, and he gets a Steelers defense that is giving up 4.3 YPC (20th). I'd expect a run-heavy approach from the Colts to start this one, but the Steelers should counter with more single-high coverages, spinning down from their split-safety shells to get numbers in the front. Look for quarterback Daniel Jones to lean on play-action throws that mirror the run game. Jones ranks fifth in play-action attempts this season, and the Colts will look to open intermediate windows against a Steelers defense that plays heavy zone coverage (75.4% of coverage snaps). And without wide receiver Alec Pierce (IR/heel), there is a missing vertical element for the Colts, as Jones' 5.7 YPA ranks 28th. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen need to uncover and make themselves available to the QB in this one, and I would like to see tight end Tyler Warren featured more on seams and corner routes to create chunk plays. Picks: Steelers -2.5 (-118), Under 44.5 (-118) Prop bets: Jonathan Taylor rushing + receiving yards OVER 105.5 (-114) I'll trust the anticipated volume for Taylor, who has had at least 21 touches in all four games played this season, producing at least 110 total yards in two. With the rushing totals and targets on screens and check downs, Taylor should hit the over. Jaylen Warren rushing yards OVER 62.5 (-112) Warren has rushed for at least 93 yards in two straight games, with 17 carries in each. Take Warren's recent run on production in a matchup versus a Colts defense allowing 4.8 YPC (sixth highest in the league). Now, let's get to some other bets I like ... Christian Watson anytime TD (+195) Watson has scored at least one touchdown in three of four games played, and he has four end zone targets on the season. Plus, we know Watson can separate over the top. I like the matchup here for the Packers' receiver against the Bears' cornerbacks, and Matt LaFleur can also scheme zone-beaters for Watson. San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks total points UNDER 45.5 (-105) In the two games these clubs played last season, the totals hit 30 and 16. Mike Macdonald has the scheme (and personnel) to limit the 49ers' offense. I'd take the under in this one. Three-team parlay (+638) Jacksonville Jaguars -7.5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles Cleveland Browns +1.5 at New York Jets Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 at New England Patriots The Jaguars might be the best team in football, and they get an Eagles squad that is going through major in-season transitions on the offensive line. Plus, Philly will be without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith . Cleveland also is playing good ball. Todd Monken's offense can take vertical shots in the pass game, and the downhill rushing attack is a foundational approach with Quinshon Judkins . The Browns can run the ball against a Jets defense that just gave up 232 yards on the ground to the Bears in Week 4. Let's finish this parlay with the Raiders getting points on the road in New England. Las Vegas features a top-10 passing defense, and quarterback Kirk Cousins is an easy fit in Klint Kubiak's schemed-up system. The Raiders need more here from Ashton Jeanty and the run game, but I like them to cover. The Giants' 2-0 run with Winston has been extremely unimpressive. They beat the Titans 12-7 on a rainy and windy day in MetLife Staduim thanks to a game-sealing end zone pick from Jevon Holland . They beat the Cardinals 36-24 thanks to a 98-yard pick-six by Deonte Banks on fourth-and-goal. With a little bit better red zone execution from two of the league's worst starting quarterbacks, the Giants are 1-3. Editor's Picks Are Texans and Chargers this bad? How should we bet the Rams? Pamela Maldonado Early bets for Week 5: Three games to target right away ESPN NFL Week 5 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game ESPN 2 Related As it is, the Giants are 27th in EPA per drive and in success rate during Winston's two starts, and they draw a plucky Commanders defense that can bring out the worst of Winston by blitzing heavily (second only to the Vikings in blitz rate) and forcing turnovers. Star receiver Malik Nabers sat out Wednesday's practice because of a sore knee, and if he is at all limited, the Giants' lack of pass-catching depth makes it challenging to move the ball with any consistency. Washington is enduring a slew of its own injuries. Receivers Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs were both absent from Wednesday's practice, and their top two running backs ( Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt ), two tight ends ( Chig Okonkwo and Ben Sinnott ), and both starting linebackers ( Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu ) were all limited. Assuming most of the rep management midweek is preventative, the Commanders have more than enough talent to get a decisive home win against an inflated divisional opponent. Quinshon Judkins rushing yards UNDER 59.5 (-114) Only once has Judkins cleared this mark, and it was a game the Browns led nearly pole-to-pole at home against the Panthers in Week 3. On Sunday, they'll face a solid Jets run defense on the road. New York's overall numbers won't look good after a 30-carry, 146-yard outing from Kyle Monangai last week, but the Jets' defense was on the field for over 44 minutes in that game. The Bears are a spectacular rushing team and enjoyed a preposterous game script. I'm willing to throw away that outcome. Judkins and the Cleveland running game simply have not been very effective. Judkins has a success rate of 27.1%, 88th out of 95 running backs with at least 15 carries. He's averaging 3.0 yards per carry, thanks in part to only 31 rushing yards before contact on the season. Unless he rips off a big one or the Browns get a dominant game script, it will be hard for him to nickel and dime his way to this number. NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Zay Flowers 6+ receptions (-109) The Zay Flowers over betting will continue until morale improves. Flowers is on a ridiculous pace to start the season. Among receivers with at least 40 routes, Flowers is first in, well, just about everything. His 6.4 yards per route run is absurd. His 16.0 yards per target is preposterous. His 44.9% target per route run rate quite literally means he is targeted on almost every other route. For perspective, Jaxon Smith-Njigba has a 39% target rate and averages 11.7 yards per target. We're getting a discounted Flowers line this week because Lamar Jackson is out. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's approach to the passing game -- funneling targets to Flowers at all costs -- will not change with Tyler Huntley in the lineup. Huntley is a solid backup and has experience working with Flowers, who has a 28.7% target rate on 80 routes across eight games with Huntley. I prefer receptions to receiving yards this week, as I imagine Flowers will get an uptick in easy designed touches to help insulate the backup quarterback, but both are live. Michael Mayer receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) We're back to the well on Mayer, who did us solid last week and is back again with another abbreviated line. Mayer is priced as if he is a TE2 to Brock Bowers ' TE1, but Bowers is functionally a wide reciever, so Mayer doesn't leave the field nearly as often as a TE2 usually does. Mayer's route share in the two weeks since Bowers returned to the lineup is 72.1%, 11th among all tight ends. It's right between Tucker Kraft and Juwan Johnson . The Raiders played 87% of their snaps last week in multiple-TE sets, and that trend isn't changing. They don't have the wide receivers to take snaps away from the tight ends. Mayer simply doesn't leave the field for passing downs. Mayer gets a tougher defensive draw this week, as the Patriots are giving up only 5.5 yards per pass attempts to tight ends (sixth lowest) and a 68.4% completion rate (seventh lowest) through the first four weeks of the season. But his line simply doesn't jibe with how often he's on the field, nor the volume at which the Raiders throw the football -- especially as an underdog on the road. I'll be taking Mayer at this line for a full unit and tracking half a unit on 40+ receiving yards at +165. NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks Kalif Raymond 4+ receptions (+123) Raymond's furious start to the season crashed with a two-catch, six-yard performance against the Jets in Week 4, creating a strong buy-low opportunity. Raymond was the deep downfield target on two Tyson Bagent would-be interceptions (both reversed on penalty) and retained a 50% route rate on Bears dropbacks. It should have been another decently productive day. With Bagent under center, there is some concern that the Bears' target distribution will shift as he discovers which receivers he likes best. But wideouts tend to catch the football against the Packers -- they are giving up a completion percentage of 70.8% to wide receivers on the season, fifth highest in football -- thanks in part to the soft coverages and easy underneath access afforded by their defensive structure. We know Ben Johnson won't shy away from a high-volume passing day, even with his backup quarterbacks, so it's fair to project Raymond closer to his Weeks 1-3 production (8, 5 and 6 catches) than his Week 4 disappearance. Tyson Bagent interceptions OVER 0.5 (-102) Bagent gave the Jets -- the Jets! -- their first interception since the 2024 season last week, and he tried to give them another three, all of which were called back because of penalties. Four would-be interceptions sounds like a lot ... and it is! Bagent had 36 dropbacks, as the Bears enormously outpossessed the Jets (89 plays to 32). But with his pass attempts line set for 31.5 this week against the Packers, we can expect him to have volume again. Bagent is a better passer than he was when he last made starts in his rookie season in 2023, and he certainly didn't enjoy the insulation of a Ben Johnson offense back then. But he was a high-interception player at that time as well, throwing six picks over 143 pass attempts. Bagent's career INT rate on dropbacks is 3.3%, eighth among all quarterbacks since 2023. He's just below Jameis Winston (3.7% INT rate), who is priced at -184 this week against the Commanders. The Packers' defense has generated four picks through four games this season. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon is blitzing more than he did in Arizona, and his wonky safety structures can bait young quarterbacks into bad throws. I'd take this out to -110. Walder's prop bets Defensive plays Los Angeles Chargers to record first sack of game (+175) Yes, the Broncos are favored. Yes, Bo Nix is very good at sack avoidance. And yes, Denver has the better offensive line. But that's not enough to swing the odds this far, at least according to my model, which prices this bet at +127. One thing working in our favor: The Chargers are very run-heavy relative to expectation based on game situation, so that could limit the number of sack opportunities for the Broncos early. Cincinnati Bengals will NOT give up a sack on their first drive (-448) The Dolphins had not recorded a single sack until last week's game against the Vikings, and I'm surprised the odds are so favorable for Cincinnati to avoid taking a sack on the first drive here. Joe Burrow has been fairly good at sack avoidance this season, with a better-than-average 5.3% sack rate behind an offensive line that is middle of the road in terms of pass block win rate -- that is, a lot better than it has been at any point in Burrow's pro career. Chop Robinson sacks OVER 0.25 (+180) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks Robinson is playing significantly more this season, especially on passing downs, and is looking much more like the player he was in the back half of his rookie season than the one who had a disappointing sophomore campaign. Robinson leads the league in pass rush win rate at edge. This line got shorter on Saturday, but there are a few factors keeping the odds decently strong: The Miami Dolphins are solid underdogs; Joe Burrow has gotten better at sack avoidance; and Cincinnati Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims is having a great season in pass protection. Those are all valid, but these odds are still good enough to bet. I'd wager this down to +145. Khalil Mack sacks OVER 0.25 (+217) Remarkably, at age 35 (!), Mack has seen a pretty significant increase in workload under new defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary as compared with the past two seasons. Mack has rushed the passer on 72% of opponent dropbacks, up from 55% a year ago. That my model likes him despite still partially factoring in last year's pass-rushing rates makes me like this bet even more. Mack's pass rush win rate is below average, but Mack has always been a player who had a higher sack to pass rush win ratio than most. While t he Broncos' Bo Nix is excellent at sack avoidance, sometimes the price is too good to pass up. I would bet this down to +138. Other sack bets I recommend: Abdul Carter sacks OVER 0.25 (+101) Lukas Van Ness sacks OVER 0.25 (+173) Dexter Lawrence II sacks UNDER 0.25 (-129) Alex Highsmith sacks UNDER 0.25 (-115) Jared Verse sacks OVER 0.25 (+171) Maliek Collins sacks UNDER 0.25 (-145) Maxx Crosby sacks OVER 0.25 (-108) Odafe Oweh sacks OVER 0.25 (+150) Tuli Tuipulotu sacks OVER 0.25 (+193) Zach Allen sacks UNDER 0.25 (+105) Keion White sacks OVER 0.25 (+297) Jaquan Brisker tackles + assists UNDER 7.5 (-138) With an 86th percentile tackle per play rate, Brisker is making tackles more often with Pittsburgh this season than with Chicago last season. Even so, he has actually only covered this line one time in four games. While most players record tackles at a higher rate against the run than the pass, Brisker has been so strong against the pass (and just mediocre against the run) that the opposite is true for him. But this week his pass-play tackling prowess could be mitigated, because the Colts are a run-leaning team. My model likes the under, and I would bet it down to -165. Jordyn Brooks tackles + assists UNDER 8.5 (+112) The Bengals made waves last week by having Joe Burrow throw 54 times and with Burrow himself requesting to throw the ball even more. The advanced numbers back up the obvious: Cincinnati is an extremely pass-heavy team, and they currently rank first in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. While a starting linebacker on a heavy-underdog team is usually a prime candidate for a huge tackling day (because the favorite gets out to a lead and then runs the ball a ton), the Bengals are so pass-heavy that the effect should be smaller here. Because we're getting plus-money, my model likes the under. I would bet this down to +105. Other tackle bets I recommend: Evan Williams tackles + assists UNDER 6.5 (+113) Fred Warner tackles + assists UNDER 8.5 (-119) Brandon Jones tackles + assists UNDER 6.5 (-113) Offensive plays David Montgomery 1.5 receptions OVER (+119) Though Montgomery's production has been disappointing, he has covered this receptions line in three of four games. That's not really why I'm backing him here. Instead, it's because the Titans play zone coverage at a league high 80%(!) clip, and running backs catch passes almost twice as frequently on dropbacks vs. zone (15% of the time since 2022) than man (8%). And based on my backtesting, that effect is not fully baked into the market. Geno Smith under 0.5 interceptions (+122) Interception props typically hover right around 50%, and it's rare to see this much plus-money on a player whose team is favored in a game and hasn't thrown an interception yet this season! Even considering Smith's play last year (when he led the league in interceptions thrown with 17), this is just too generous a price. That the Jets have been a run-leaning team thus far in 2026 also helps. I have seven picks I like this week, including player props on Patrick Mahomes , Drake Maye , and Tony Pollard , plus three spreads picks for the 1 PM Eastern games. Best of luck, happy November, and enjoy your day! Vikings at Lions (-3): O/U 46.5 I said Monday of this week on NBC that this was the no-brainer of the week. It’s a miracle that the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the NFL, and to me, they are the most overrated team. In the last four games, Minnesota has beaten Tampa Bay, Miami, New Orleans, and Indianapolis; those teams are a combined 7-20. Last season, the Vikings swept the Lions in the regular season, and adding Kyler Murray likely doesn’t equate to another sweep over Detroit. Murray ranks 21st and 26th in passer rating against man and zone coverage, 28th in blitzed completion percentage (54.8%), and 26th in play-action completion percentage (54.9%). On early downs, Minnesota ranks in success rate, while Detroit is first. Going score for score on the road as an underdog with Jared Goff and the Lions doesn’t seem plausible to me. I like Detroit -3 at -120 odds. Pick: Lions -3 (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Titans at Bengals (-12.5): O/U 46.5 Tony Pollard had a season-high 129 rushing yards on 25 carries and tied a career-high with three rushing touchdowns. It was a great day for Pollard, but the Titans lost at the buzzer 27-24 to the Browns. Now, Tennessee goes on the road as double-digit underdogs in Cincinnati. Not a recipe for success. Last week, Pollard had an amazing game script to be fed, maybe the best he’s had all year, but I don’t see it this week, especially going up against Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen . The Bengals held Derrick Henry to 45 rushing yards on 17 carries last week, and with Cam Ward striking no fear in the Bengals’ hearts, I’d think Cincy stacks the box and attempt to take Pollard out of the equation. I went Under 65.5 rushing yards on Pollard and would go down to 60.5. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 65.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Browns at Steelers (-3.5): O/U 38.5 I still can’t believe my eyes and ears regarding the Cleveland Browns being 5-2! But all good things must come to an end, right? All five of Cleveland’s wins have come by four or fewer points, and they needed a walkoff field goal to beat the Titans in Tennessee and the same at home against the Ravens in the last two weeks. Cleveland has been playing with fire recently, while the Steelers were spotted flying back from Paris playing with ice. Aaron Rodgers was wearing chains that cost more than my house and probably yours too on that flight back from the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris. Rodgers said it was his favorite road flight of his lengthy NFL career, and the Steelers are starting to hit their stride with three-straight wins following the loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers traveling back to an immediate game is worrisome because the last eight teams that played in London, then a game in the States the following week, went 0-8 ATS! However, the Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. It’s a revenge spot for Pittsburgh, and if you’ve seen the back-and-forth between Cam Heyward and Jared Verse this week, then you know it’s going to be a classic AFC North slugfest. Give me Pittsburgh at home -3.5. I’d prefer a -3, but the sportsbooks are playing more defense than ever this season. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (1 unit) Falcons at Bucs (-2.5): O/U Tampa Bay got that Baker bump last week! Baker Mayfield came back from injury and Tampa Bay looked inspired. The Bucs rattled Bryce Young last week and destroyed his confidence turning three turnovers into 17 of the teams 43 points. This week won’t be so easy hosting Atlanta in a letdown spot off the hype. Mayfield only threw the ball 11 times, so we truly don’t know how healthy he is or how effective he will be, but we know what to expect from Atlanta. The Falcons have the fifth-best offensive success rate since Michael Penix has taken over, and he’s gotten the ball out quick with 50% of his passes coming within 2.5 seconds (fourth-best). That could be the key against a blitz and pressure heavy Bucs defense. Tampa Bay loads the box with eight or more players at the second-highest clip (22.1%) and blitzes 40.4% of the time when doing so, which ranks fifth-most. I’d expect a lot of screens, draws, and quick throws to offeset the Bucs defense, while Atlanta likely brings pressure and tries to hit Mayfield as many times as possible to truly test his health and conditioning. Give me Atlanta. Pick: Falcons +2.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Patriots (-7) at Dolphins: O/U 43.5 Last season, Drake Maye completed 33-of-41 (80.5%) passes for 421 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions over two wins against Miami. Maye even added 72 rushing yards and another score on 15 carries in those two outings. This Miami defense is even less menacing than last year. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, and two came in Week 1 against Kirk Cousins , with another last week courtesy of Geno Smith . When Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes , Brock Purdy , and Kyler Murray played Miami, that group averaged 242.5 passing yards against the Dolphins and combined for eight touchdown passes to one interception. Kyler Murray was the only quarterback who hasn’t thrown at least two touchdowns against Miami. At -102 odds, I like Maye to go Under 0.5 Interceptions versus Miami for a third consecutive time and like 2+ Pass touchdowns for parlays. Pick: Drake Maye Under 0.5 Interceptions (1 unit) Chiefs (-1.5) at Broncos: O/U 40.5 In Week 1 against Denver, Patrick Mahomes came back from a major surgery and finished with 184 passing yards, 15-of-27 passing, and three total touchdowns, including an epic rushing score to start the game. He went Under all of his props except passing touchdowns and rushing yards. Fast forward to last week, Mahomes had his worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks in Seattle. Mahomes turns around and goes to Denver to face a Broncos defense that almost went to the Super Bowl. It’s going to be a long day for the Chiefs, but unless Kenneth Walker goes crazy again (191 total yards, 2 TDs) this looks like a spot for Mahomes to go over his props. The Broncos average 5.1 plays per possession, ranking worst in the NFL. That’s one area that points toward more plays and possessions for the Chiefs. Both of these teams rarely allow sacks or turn the ball over, so we should see plenty of possessions. Both teams had 12 drives in Week 1’s meeting, and Kansas City ran 20 more plays than Denver (62-42) thanks to the running game, and it was Davis Webb ‘s first game as an OC with the Broncos. Still, Kansas City will likely run more plays and have more possessions than Denver. Denver got back Jonathan Cooper last week, plus Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga could both play today. The Denver defense has usually limited the touchdown damage through the air from Mahomes, but in order to move the ball against Denver’s defense, Mahomes will have to be actively taking what the Broncos can give him. I like Mahomes to go Over 20.5 completions and 220.5 paassing yards up to 21.5 and 225.5. I lean his Over pass attempts. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . 49ers @ Cowboys I think wagering on a side or total for a Cowboys game is a foolish decision. You never know what you’re getting from this team. What I do know about this game is that the 49ers will use Christian McCaffrey as they normally do. CMC had 18 carries last week and an additional three targets through the air. That’s 21 attempts to gain yards in a game the Niners won by multiple touchdowns. In the last two close games the 49ers have played, CMC got 16 carries and 10 targets. I’d imagine this game will see the 49ers looking to put up some numbers, as the Cowboys' offense will probably look to do the same, since the defense can't … defend. The Dallas defense ranks 31st against the rush, and it is middle-of-the-pack in receiving yards allowed to running backs. However, Dallas doesn’t face many teams that want to pass to the running back as much as the 49ers do. Geoff Schwartz likes Christian McCaffrey to have a productive Week 10 (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images). Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 99.5 rushing and receiving yards Vikings @ Packers Can Kirk Cousins lead the Vikings past the scorching-hot Packers in his first game back with Minnesota? (David Berding/Getty Images). The Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to help fix their offensive woes. He’s an immediate upgrade over what the Vikings had at QB with Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray. And while Cousins is probably average at best right now, that’s all the Vikings need at that position. The Vikings’ defense and special teams are elite. Minnesota just needs an offense that can move the ball enough to score points, so the defense doesn’t have to be perfect to win games. This move might actually allow the Vikings’ defense to play even better. The Packers have been outstanding at throwing down the field. Jordan Love has been bombing the ball to his receivers, and although the rushing game isn’t great, Green Bay is scoring enough points. The defense has also played better than expected, shutting down nearly every offense it has faced this season. I like the Vikings to cover this game for a few reasons. For starters, just having Cousins in the lineup will reinvigorate the Vikings, and it wouldn’t surprise me to see Justin Jefferson have his best game of the season. I also like the matchup of the Vikings’ defense against the Packers’ offensive line, which is mediocre. Minnesota's pressure packages will be difficult to handle. articles.text: Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Thursday Night Football Betting Picks Fantasy Advice --> --> Betting Picks Fantasy Advice Betting Picks All Sports Betting Picks NFL Picks NBA Picks MLB Picks NHL Picks College Football Picks College Basketball Picks Soccer Picks Golf Picks UFC Picks WNBA Picks Tennis Picks NASCAR Picks Boxing Picks Fantasy Advice All Fantasy Advice NFL Fantasy NBA Fantasy MLB Fantasy NHL Fantasy Golf Fantasy UFC Fantasy WNBA Fantasy NASCAR Fantasy Pick6 Season Long Best Ball Sports NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Soccer Golf UFC WNBA NASCAR Tennis Boxing Wrestling Betting Tools Betting Splits Most Bet Player Props Parlays Odds, Lines & Spreads NFL Player Prop Trends Tracker NBA Player Prop Trends Tracker MLB Player Prop Trends Tracker NRFI Tracker NFL Trending Parlay Picks Optimizer News & More News Sportsbook Insights How to Watch Podcasts DKN Shows How to Bet Jackpocket Casino Entertainment All Entertainment TV & Film Movie Reviews Marvel Cinematic Universe Star Wars Pro Wrestling Trading Cards Sneaker Drops DKN Español Settings Toggle dark mode Dark Mode Betting Splits Player Props NFL Parlay Builder Sports Betting Picks Fantasy Advice Start/Sit Advice NBA Parlay Builder NFL SGP Betting Tool Parlays Odds, Lines & Spreads Entertainment DKN Español > --> Home NFL Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Thursday Night Football Dallas Cowboys Sports Betting Picks NFL DraftKings Sportsbook Insights Player Props Updated: September 17, 2026 By: Sean Barnard Week 2 of NFL action kicks off with a thrilling Thursday Night Football battle between the Detroit Lions and the Buffalo Bills. Both teams have deep playoff aspirations and picked up Week 1 victories. The Bills fended off the Texans 36-31, while the Lions were pushed to the limit in a 31-30 overtime victory against the Saints. They will now square off in a measuring stick matchup against each other to kick off the second week of the season. Looking at the odds, the Bills enter as 5.5-point favorites with -230 Moneyline odds on DraftKings Sportsbook . The Lions hold +190 odds to pull off the upset, with the game total set at 54.5 points. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> But there are plenty of ways to get involved in the action beyond backing a side or total. Let’s take a look at my top three favorite player props for the Week 2 Thursday Night Football matchup. RELATED NFL Injury Report: Latest Updates for Week 2 Lions vs. Bills NFL Player Prop Bets for Thursday Night Football Dalton Kincaid Over 50.5 Receiving Yards (-111) The Buffalo Bills added D.J. Moore this offseason to provide Josh Allen with a top wide receiver threat. But the star quarterback has traditionally leaned heavily on his tight ends for production through the air, and the opening week matchup proved this is not fully changing. Dalton Kincaid led all Bills’ pass catchers, pulling in five of his six targets for 130 total yards. Kincaid averaged 47.6 yards per game through the air last year, and has tallied 1,692 receiving yards through the first three years of his career. This is a great opportunity to build off this, as the Detroit Lions’ defense looked like it could be carved up by an adequate high school team in the season opener. The New Orleans Saints marched down the field with little resistance, putting up 469 total yards of offense and scoring 30 points in the matchup. This includes 378 yards through the air, and both tight ends were heavily involved in the attack. Juwan Johnson pulled in three receptions on seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown, while Noah Fant added four receptions on eight targets for 33 yards and a score of his own The Bills lean on Kincaid at an even greater rate than the Saints do in their offensive attack, and he is a superior talent to the New Orleans tight ends. While the 130 yard output is not sustainable to repeat at a frequent rate, count on him remaining a key part of the gameplan and a safety valve for Allen throughout. Detroit should improve to some extent in their pass defense, but the matchup problem at the tight end position was evident in Week 1, and this is a difficult fix on a short week. Count on Kincaid remaining heavily involved in the Bills’ offense, and for over 50.5 receiving yards to be a comfortable bar to clear. Josh Allen Over 253.5 Passing Yards (-111) The 2024 NFL MVP got off to a strong start to this season, throwing for 334 yards on just 29 pass attempts against the Houston Texans. This is a Texans’ defense that finished last season ranked second in opponents’ points allowed, first in yards conceded, and sixth in opponents’ passing yards last season. They were widely expected to have a case for one of the top defensive units in football this year, but will need to make some major improvements from their Week 1 performance if this is to be the case. But the impressive output should say more about Allen than the Texans’ defense. The Bills’ star had a bit of a down season last year in his passing metrics, averaging 215.8 passing yards per game. But he is averaging 235.9 passing yards per game in his career and tallied as many as 284.0 over a season. Allen still tallied 253 passing yards or greater in seven games ,even with it being a down year in passing production last year. Allen will also be able to feast on this Lions’ defense, given the concerns mentioned above. Tyler Shough aired the ball out for 410 passing yards and three touchdowns against them last week to provide the upset scare. Even if you are not the biggest Allen fan, it is difficult to argue against the four-time Pro Bowler having significantly more arm talent than Shough. With better receiving talent around him and holes across this Detroit defense, expect plenty of passing success and for the 253.5 passing yard line not to be nearly high enough. Run defense was a concern for the Bills coming into the season, as they finished last year ranked 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed, 31st in rushing touchdowns conceded, and 30th in net yards per rush attempts. Gibbs has game-breaking speed and can take any given carry the length of the field for a touchdown score. With no real competition looking over his shoulder for carries, expect plenty of these chances and for the 24-year-old to find the open field at least once. He has tallied over 90.5 rushing yards in 13 games already in his career, and is receiving the largest opportunity in the offense thus far. Count on the Lions continuing to make it a clear effort to put the ball in the star running back’s hands and for Gibbs to have success against this porous defense. Back the Lions’ star to record over 90.5 rushing yards for the second straight week, and don’t be fully surprised if he exceeds last week’s massive 156 yard rushing output.
